carousels.go_deeper: A prayer for comfort in grief

slides.headline: Missing someone this Christmas?
slides.sub: A few gentle words for a hard season.

slides.heading: There’s no right way to grieve.
body: Grief isn’t a problem to solve or a test of faith to pass.
Let yourself feel what you feel, lean on others, and give yourself time.

slides.quote: Yahweh is near to those who have a broken heart, and saves those who have a crushed spirit.
slides.note: You don’t have to reach God. He comes close.

slides.quote: You count my wanderings. You put my tears into your container. Aren’t they in your book?
slides.note: Every tear is counted and kept.

slides.heading: On anniversaries and holidays
body: Father, today the empty chair feels louder. Help me honor them, let myself feel the loss, and find moments of grace even here.

slides.close: Be gentle with yourself this season.

carousels.kicker: How to read the Bible in a year
carousels.go_deeper: How to read the Bible in a year

slides.headline: How to read the Bible in 2027.
slides.sub: A little over three chapters a day, and what to do when you miss one.

slides.heading: How many chapters a day is it?
body: 1,189 chapters divided by 365 days is about 3.3 chapters a day.

slides.heading: There’s no wrong choice.
body: The best plan is the one you’ll still be reading in March.
Attach it to something you already do, like morning coffee, a lunch break, or the last thing before bed.

slides.heading: What if you fall behind?
body: Just read today’s reading and keep going.
And if a year turns into fourteen months, you’ve still read the whole Bible.

slides.quote: Open my eyes, that I may see wondrous things out of your law.
slides.note: Read for the story, not for perfect understanding.

slides.close: Start any day of the year.

posts.caption: What does the Bible say about waiting on God? Psalm 130:5–6: “I wait for Yahweh. My soul waits. I hope in his word. My soul longs for the Lord more than watchmen long for the morning, more than watchmen for the morning.” Advent is a season of waiting. In Hebrew poetry, waiting and hoping are the same posture: leaning forward toward God. More Bible verses about hope, from Worship Room: worshiproom.com/guides/bible-verses-about-hope #advent #bibleverse #hope #christiantiktok

What to pray when you can’t sleep. Psalm 121:4: “Behold, he who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.” God keeps watch while you sleep. A prayer for tomorrow: Father, tomorrow is already in Your hands. Whatever it holds, You’ll be there before I am. Give me sleep tonight and strength for the morning. More short prayers for sleepless nights, from Worship Room: worshiproom.com/guides/what-to-pray-when-you-cant-sleep #prayer #cantsleep #bibleverse #christiantiktok

What to pray when you’re grieving at Christmas. When the empty chair feels louder, you can pray: Father, help me honor them, let myself feel the loss, and find moments of grace even here. “Yahweh is near to those who have a broken heart, and saves those who have a crushed spirit.” Psalm 34:18. There’s no right way to grieve. Be gentle with yourself this season. More prayers for comfort in grief, from Worship Room: worshiproom.com/guides/prayer-for-grief If you’re in crisis, call or text 988. #grief #prayer #christmas #christiantiktok

What does the Bible say about overthinking? Psalm 94:18–19: “When I said, “My foot is slipping!” Your loving kindness, Yahweh, held me up. In the multitude of my thoughts within me, your comforts delight my soul.” The psalmist had a multitude of thoughts too. God’s comfort met him in the middle of them, not after they stopped. More Bible verses for anxiety, from Worship Room: worshiproom.com/guides/bible-verses-about-anxiety #bibleverses #anxiety #overthinking #christiantiktok

What does the Bible say about feeling alone? Isaiah 49:15: “Can a woman forget her nursing child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? Yes, these may forget, yet I will not forget you!” The holidays can make loneliness louder. Even if the people closest to you forget, God says He will not. More Bible verses for loneliness, and a prayer for when you feel alone, from Worship Room: worshiproom.com/guides/bible-verses-about-loneliness #bibleverse #loneliness #christmas #christiantiktok

What is Christmas really about? 1 John 4:9: “By this God’s love was revealed in us, that God has sent his only born Son into the world that we might live through him.” Love is defined by what God did, not by how well we love Him back. More Bible verses about God’s love, from Worship Room: worshiproom.com/guides/gods-love-bible-verses #christmas #godslove #bibleverse #christiantiktok

What did the angel say to the shepherds? Luke 2:10–11: “Don’t be afraid, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy which will be to all the people. For there is born to you today, in David’s city, a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.” In Scripture, “Don’t be afraid” is almost always followed by a reason, usually God’s presence. At Christmas, the reason has a name. More Bible verses for when you’re afraid, from Worship Room: worshiproom.com/guides/bible-verses-about-fear #christmas #luke2 #bibleverse #christiantiktok

How to read the Bible in a year: about 3.3 chapters a day, 10 to 15 minutes for most people. Pick a plan, pick a time of day, and when you miss a day, just pick up with today’s reading. “Open my eyes, that I may see wondrous things out of your law.” Psalm 119:18. The full guide, from Worship Room: worshiproom.com/guides/how-to-read-the-bible-in-a-year #bibleinayear #biblereading #newyear #christiantiktok
